submissions.title: University of Oregon Institute for Policy Research & Engagement
submissions.oneLine: White paper arguing Oregon should treat economic development as a core state priority and shift to a centralized, Governor-led ecosystem model, drawing lessons from five case-study states.

submissions.title: Oregon State Board of Agriculture
submissions.oneLine: Letter to Governor Kotek supporting the Prosperity Roadmap and requesting an Agriculture/Food & Beverage representative be appointed to the Prosperity Council.

submissions.title: Oregon Workforce Partnership
submissions.oneLine: Policy brief proposing eight actions to align Oregon's workforce system (WTDB, LWDBs, WorkSource) with the Prosperity Roadmap and create employer-led Regional Industry Councils.

submissions.title: NXTClean Fuels (Governor Tina Kotek support letter)
submissions.oneLine: Governor Tina Kotek's letter to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers urging full and timely federal review of the $3B NXTClean Fuels renewable diesel/SAF facility at Port Westward.

submissions.title: Oregon State University — Prosperity Roadmap Alignment Memo
submissions.oneLine: Memo from OSU President Jayathi Murthy on how OSU's talent development, research-to-company translation, and statewide Extension presence align with and can strengthen execution of the Prosperity Roadmap.

submissions.title: Oregon Business & Industry — Cover Letter (DHM Voter Survey)
submissions.oneLine: Cover note from OBI President & CEO Angela Wilhelms transmitting a DHM Research statewide voter survey on Oregon's economy, taxes, and regulations ahead of the 2026 legislative session.

submissions.title: DHM Research — 2026 Legislative Voter Survey (for OBI)
submissions.oneLine: DHM Research executive-summary memo plus survey-result slides of OBI's 2026 legislative voter poll, showing pessimism on state direction, economy, taxes and regulation, and majority preference for a pro-growth strategy.

submissions.title: Pacific Power
submissions.oneLine: Proposes a Commission-led study framework for financially healthy utilities and rate certainty, covering wildfire policy (wildfire fund, liability limits) and regulatory certainty/efficiency for electric energy infrastructure investment.

submissions.title: Westside Economic Alliance (Industrial Land Readiness Workgroup)
submissions.oneLine: Memorandum summarizing the Industrial Land Readiness Workgroup's recommendations to Metro to align buildable industrial land methodology with market realities and support regional economic development.

submissions.title: Lois Neistat (Individual / Concerned Oregonians)
submissions.oneLine: Individual's policy critique listing problems (regulation, taxes, K-12, PERS, land use) and goals, recommending eliminating recent regulations to retain and attract companies in Oregon.

submissions.title: SEDCOR (email forwarded by Lois Cho, CHO Wines)
submissions.oneLine: SEDCOR's Abisha Romano forwards examples (Chapul Farms, Estate Bakery, hazelnut biomass, BOLI/Davis-Bacon prevailing wage) of how the state could better support business innovation and streamline regulation.

submissions.title: Lois Cho, CHO Wines (Governor's Prosperity Council member)
submissions.oneLine: Lois Cho's Meeting #2 contribution summarizing wine-industry and EDO stakeholder outreach, with themes on fragmentation, workforce/housing, land use, marketing, and cautious recommendations using existing structures.

submissions.title: Portland Metro Chamber — 2026 State Legislative Action Plan
submissions.oneLine: Portland Metro Chamber 2026 State Legislative Action Plan arguing Portland's economic health is a smart statewide investment, with priorities on sports/arts venues, circular economy, workforce, business recruitment, and housing.

submissions.title: Portland Metro Chamber — 2026 Regional Policy Agenda
submissions.oneLine: Portland Metro Chamber 2026 Regional Policy Agenda outlining priorities for economic growth, tax competitiveness, housing, public safety, and climate in the Portland metro region.

submissions.title: Alice Dale (SEIU Labor Consultant)
submissions.oneLine: Outline of an 'Oregon's High Road Economic Strategy' arguing for high-wage/high-skill growth, education investment (40/40/20), and against ineffective tax incentives.

submissions.title: Oregon Business Council
submissions.oneLine: Letter to the Governor's Prosperity Council ('A Moment of Economic Reckoning') warning of structural stagnation and proposing five structural priorities for Oregon's economic renewal.

submissions.title: Portland Seed Fund
submissions.oneLine: March 19, 2026 letter to Governor Kotek urging a line-item veto of the SB 1507 QSBS provision, signed by general partners and 43 portfolio company signatories.

submissions.title: Oregon Tech Entrepreneurs & Investors
submissions.oneLine: Letter to Governor Kotek urging a veto of SB 1507 to preserve Oregon's QSBS tax exclusion, arguing the bill would drive founders and investors out of state and lose far more revenue than it raises; signed by dozens of Oregon tech founders and investors.

submissions.title: Energy Trust of Oregon — Survey Response Memo (Chris Lyons)
submissions.oneLine: Memo transmitting Energy Trust of Oregon's responses to the Prosperity Council survey, focused on clean energy workforce development needs, coordination gaps, and the economic benefits of energy efficiency investment.

submissions.title: Clean and Resilient Economy Contributors
submissions.oneLine: Draft economic development strategy deck proposing Oregon formally designate a 'Clean & Resilient Economy' priority traded-sector platform with coordinated innovation, capital, workforce, and resilience architecture.

submissions.title: Portland Metro Chamber — Tax Reform & Regional Economy Letter
submissions.oneLine: Letter urging tax reform, traded-sector competitiveness, housing production, and regulatory modernization, citing its State of the Regional Economy report.

submissions.title: Tillamook County Creamery Association
submissions.oneLine: Survey-response submission on regulatory coherence, farmworker overtime, recycling EPR fees, rural childcare/housing, and competitive investment incentives.

submissions.title: Jordan Papé, CEO, The Papé Group (Individual, Eugene)
submissions.oneLine: Position paper arguing Oregon's man-made policies (high tax, land use, regulation, weak K-12) deter investment, with proposed fixes.

submissions.title: Oregon Business & Industry — Policy Recommendations Memo
submissions.oneLine: Memo of recommendations to reduce policy-outlier laws, lower costs, build a 'culture of yes,' and prioritize economic development.

submissions.title: Jacqueline Danos (Individual, Yachats, Oregon)
submissions.oneLine: Resident urges the Council to redefine prosperity beyond GDP, investing in people, education, small/regenerative farms and local sustainable industries rather than chasing large corporations.

submissions.title: Central Oregon LandWatch (Ben Gordon, Executive Director)
submissions.oneLine: Argues Oregon's 50-year land use program is the foundation of the state's economic vitality and 'second paycheck,' urging the Council to uphold its key pillars.

submissions.title: Alice Dale (SEIU Labor Consultant) & Robert Camarillo (Oregon State Building & Construction Trades Council)
submissions.oneLine: 17-page 'High Road to Prosperity' report arguing for raising per-capita income, education/workforce investment, worker-centered AI guardrails, and skepticism of tax incentives and business-climate rankings.

submissions.title: Microsoft Corporation (Hana Doubrava, Director, Cascadia)
submissions.oneLine: Cover letter plus recommendations expressing support for the Prosperity Roadmap and offering Microsoft AI programs for research, AI literacy, workforce data, and AI-enabled job preparation.

submissions.title: Energy Trust of Oregon — Survey Form Response
submissions.oneLine: Energy Trust of Oregon's responses to Governor Kotek's Prosperity Council survey, focused on clean energy workforce development barriers and a proposed statewide clean energy workforce strategy.

submissions.title: Coalition of Oregon Employer and Business Associations (Oregon Employer Coalition)
submissions.oneLine: Coalition letter urging the Council to preserve Oregon's stable, affordable workers' compensation system and SAIF Corporation as an economic asset.

submissions.title: Move Oregon Forward — Cover Letter
submissions.oneLine: Cover letter transmitting the 'Smarter Investing in Transportation' report and arguing that transportation policy is economic policy.

submissions.title: Move Oregon Forward — Report
submissions.oneLine: 'Smarter Investing in Transportation for a Stronger Oregon Economy' report making the economic case for maintenance, transit, active transportation, safety, and electrification over road expansion.

submissions.title: Oregon Association of Nurseries
submissions.oneLine: Memo recommending labor/overtime alignment, tax code review, CTE workforce funding, and climate/EPR reform to support the nursery and greenhouse industry.

submissions.title: Keith Wilson (Mayor, City of Portland) & Andrew Hoan (Portland Metro Chamber) — Cascadia High-Speed Rail advocates
submissions.oneLine: Letter urging the Council to adopt Cascadia high-speed rail as a cornerstone long-term economic development and workforce-mobility strategy for Oregon.

submissions.title: Oregon Forest Industries Council
submissions.oneLine: Memorandum recommending the forest products sector be treated as a priority traded sector, with cost/predictability reforms, Private Forest Accord durability, mass timber support, and active forest management.

submissions.title: Oregon Winegrowers Association
submissions.oneLine: Letter recommending stronger state promotion of the wine industry, reduced tax/EPR cost burdens, and regulatory/permitting relief for wineries and vineyards.

submissions.title: Oregon Public University Presidents
submissions.oneLine: Memo to Prosperity Council co-chairs with five recommendations to sustain public university funding, engage universities in economic development, build workforce-aligned investment pools, and invest in research/innovation.

submissions.title: Oregon State University — President Murthy Email
submissions.oneLine: Forwarded email urging the state to sustain university budgets, develop workforce-aligned investment pools, and bolster Oregon's research/innovation economy (UIRF, University Venture Development Fund, Innovation Corridor, CorMic Tech Hub).

submissions.title: Oregon Public Universities
submissions.oneLine: Slide deck on the statewide economic impact and ROI of public universities ($1=$10), the future of work, funding context, state vs. student funding share, and rising personnel/OPE costs.

submissions.title: The Pew Charitable Trusts (U.S. Conservation project, Brett Swift)
submissions.oneLine: Letter urging the Council to call for an independent permitting analysis, reinvest in state/local land-use planning capacity (e.g. Oregon Coastal Management Program), align with climate executive orders, and engage ODOE's Natural Climate Solutions program.

submissions.title: Our Oregon (coalition of ~31 labor/community organizations and individuals, incl. SEIU Oregon, Oregon Labor Federation, OCPP)
submissions.oneLine: Coalition letter arguing the Council's draft recommendations deliver prosperity for corporations and the wealthy rather than working families, and rejecting tax cuts, deregulation, and corporate incentives as trickle-down economics.

submissions.title: Oregon Semiconductor Industry Coalition
submissions.oneLine: Policy brief with six priorities to strengthen Oregon's semiconductor competitiveness: Corporate Activity Tax reform, emissions cost protection, streamlined air-toxics permitting, affordability/workforce retention, preserving incentives (SIP), and higher-education investment.

submissions.title: Oregon Farm Bureau (Angela Bailey, President)
submissions.oneLine: Response to the Prosperity Roadmap urging that production agriculture be explicitly recognized as a priority economic sector, with regional agricultural highlights, regulatory and tax reform asks, and processing-capacity recommendations.

submissions.title: Oregon Trails Coalition (Steph Noll)
submissions.oneLine: Letter asking the Council to invest in Oregon's outdoor recreation economy by reinstating the Office of Outdoor Recreation and funding a world-class statewide Signature Trail network.

submissions.title: Building Resilience Coalition
submissions.oneLine: Cover letter plus attached brief 'Smarter Investing in Buildings for a Stronger Oregon Economy' arguing building electrification, energy efficiency, and community resilience are economic policies that cut costs, create trades jobs, and broaden Oregon prosperity.

submissions.title: Wild Salmon Center
submissions.oneLine: Letter urging the Prosperity Council to make protection of natural resources, cold clean water, healthy forests, outdoor recreation, and the restoration economy foundational to Oregon's statewide economic strategy.

submissions.title: Tax Fairness Oregon
submissions.oneLine: Letter reacting to draft recommendations: supports elevating economic development and regulatory review, opposes across-the-board tax cuts and wasteful data-center/tax-haven incentives, and calls for investment in higher education and infrastructure.
